Class BalpAuditEventHelper

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.ihe.fhir.support.audit.model.BalpAuditEventHelper
public abstract class BalpAuditEventHelper extends Object
What is needed to build a BALP AuditEvent but is not itself part of a BALP profile: reading the ATNA AuditMessage of a transaction, and mapping an active participant that stands for a security token to an agent. The profiles themselves are expressed by BalpAuditEvent and its subclasses.
Author:
Christian Ohr

    • findActiveParticipant

      public static Optional<ActiveParticipantType> findActiveParticipant(AuditMessage auditMessage, ActiveParticipantRoleIdCode roleIdCode)
      Looks up the active participant an agent slice is to be built from. It may be missing: an audit dataset is not guaranteed to know both ends of the transaction, and an audit record without one of the agents is still better than none at all.
      Parameters:
      auditMessage - audit message to search
      roleIdCode - role of the wanted active participant
      Returns:
      the first active participant with that role, if there is one

    • networkType

      public static AuditEvent.AuditEventAgentNetworkType networkType(ActiveParticipantType activeParticipant)
      Parameters:
      activeParticipant - active participant
      Returns:
      the network type of the given active participant, or null if it has none. The network access point type code is optional in ATNA, so it must not be dereferenced blindly -- doing so used to fail the transaction being audited.

    • reference

      public static Reference reference(String participantObjectId)
      Turns the ID of a participant object into a reference that identifies rather than merely names what it points at. BALP exists for records that hold a well-formed indication of the patient, and PIXm makes the point explicit by requiring entity.what.identifier; a display string would leave a reader to parse the identifier back out of prose.

      Five shapes occur:

      • a FHIR token, system|value, which is what the FHIR transactions record
      • a conditional reference such as Patient?identifier=system|value, which is all a conditional update or delete may know of the resource it acted on
      • a CX, value^^^&oid&ISO, which is what HL7v2 and XDS record
      • a literal reference such as Patient/a2
      • a bare id such as a document OID or a SubmissionSet UUID, which has no system to go with it but is an identifier all the same -- as the generic translation also treats it
      Parameters:
      participantObjectId - ID of a participant object, may be null
      Returns:
      a reference to what it identifies

    • requestId

      public static Optional<String> requestId(AuditMessage auditMessage)
      The value travels with the message rather than being read back out of the participant object it was encoded into, because which participant object that is depends on the profile that asked for the correlation -- IHE BALP and the Swiss EPR disagree on the code -- while the value does not.
      Parameters:
      auditMessage - audit message to read
      Returns:
      the id correlating the audit records of the two ends of the transaction, if the request carried one. BALP reports it as the transaction entity of the AuditEvent.

    • oAuthActiveParticipantToAgent

      public static Optional<AuditEvent.AuditEventAgentComponent> oAuthActiveParticipantToAgent(ActiveParticipantType ap)
      Maps an active participant that stands for a security token -- an OAuth user, an OAuth client or an opaque token -- to the user agent of an AuditEvent. Shared with the generic translation so that the profiled AuditEvents report the same user, which their profiles allow as the user agent slice.
      Parameters:
      ap - active participant
      Returns:
      the agent it maps to, or empty if it does not stand for a token
